title: Der keayboard manager zeigt Tastenumbelegungen älterer versionen an, führt sie auch aus, aber neue Umbelegungen  in dieser Form kann man nicht mehr anlegen.

fix_assessment.rationale: A scoped editor collection-policy correction is supported by exact-method execution and existing chord representation. This is a lightweight proposal, not an adversarial full design or installed-product signoff.

judgment.rationale: The supplied legacy/new screenshot and exact-method controls support an editor chord-construction regression. Apps/Menu being an action key is expected in the current model; the narrower problem is that dropdown mutation cannot preserve or append a supported second action key. The reported runtime precedence and outgoing-chord semantics need independent verification and must not be silently bundled into a modifier redesign.
judgment.recommended_action: Verify and restore incoming-chord dropdown creation/editing without classifying Apps/Menu as a modifier; test overlapping legacy/new shortcuts separately.
evidence: The German report supplies PowerToys0.102.3001, Windows11 build26300.9818, explicit dropdown reproduction and a screenshot showing legacy Shift(Right)+Apps/Menu+X/W/O/N/T mappings alongside a newly created Shift(Right)+Apps/Menu text mapping.

The reporter says legacy mappings remain visible, but new dropdown selections stop at Apps/Menu and the shorter new mapping takes precedence. No configuration export or installed runtime reproduction was supplied/executed.

Helpers.GetKeyType classifies only Win/Ctrl/Alt/Shift as modifiers; Apps/Menu is an action key. Shortcut.SetKeyCodes separately supports a first actionKey and a secondKey, so treating Apps/Menu as a new modifier is not required to investigate the existing chord representation.

The inspected UnifiedMappingControl has AllowChords and hook chord handling, but HandleAutoGrowShrink unconditionally removes trailing entries after selecting any action key and only grows after a modifier.

Three executed controls on the exact extracted collection-mutation method reproduce modifier growth, no extra field after Apps/Menu, and removal of X from an existing Shift(Right)+Apps/Menu+X list when Apps/Menu is selected. Key classification is stubbed from inspected native behavior; this is not installed UI/hook execution.

Related issue22752 requests Apps/Menu as a general modifier; issue31891 requests outgoing chords. Those enhancements are separate from restoring creation/editing of already representable incoming chords. Issue49085 concerns Allow chords state persistence, not this exact dropdown truncation.
The later Product-Keyboard Manager label is a routing update only; the complete refreshed body, comments and timeline contain no new reproduction or covering fix.

reproduce.version_requirement: Reported0.102.3001 and a supported test build with the editor correction
setup: Prepare a legacy Shift(Right)+Apps/Menu+X mapping and a shorter Shift(Right)+Apps/Menu text mapping with visibly different harmless outputs. Keep them separately enabled until the overlap step.
steps: 1. With incoming chords enabled, select Shift(Right), Apps/Menu, then X through dropdowns; compare keyboard capture.
2. Edit Apps/Menu in an existing three-key mapping, save and reopen; check whether X is preserved.
3. Repeat with chords disabled and a normal modifier-plus-one-action shortcut; check the intended one-action behavior.
4. Execute legacy and shorter mappings separately, then together; record key press/release order and actual output without assuming simultaneous/sequence semantics.
5. Verify action-side behavior remains unchanged; do not enable outgoing chords or change modifier classification implicitly.
prerequisites: Isolated interactive Windows setup; use disposable mappings or a backed-up test configuration, not the reporter production remaps.
reproduce.title: Verify legacy incoming chord creation and shorter-mapping overlap
reproduce.expected_result: Supported incoming chords can be created and round-tripped without silently dropping the second action; disabled/ordinary mappings retain current contracts. Any shorter-prefix precedence defect is reproduced and assessed separately.

initial_investigation: Read complete report/discussion/labels and linked timeline, inspected the supplied screenshot, and searched related Apps/Menu and chord work. No covering fix for this exact editor regression was established.

Read exact source at 67ac3d8b1f0fe78a649a59bdc74c29b40d3bb7f5 for Helpers.GetKeyType, Shortcut.SetKeyCodes, UnifiedMappingControl and key-hook chord handling. Related release tag0.102.2911 also contains this auto-grow method; exact reported0.102.3001 release-source identity was not established.

Compiled and executed the extracted HandleAutoGrowShrink method under the exclusive build lease with classification controls. Three cases confirm collection truncation without creating an installed-product execution claim.

Separated incoming chord edit regression, Apps/Menu-as-modifier enhancement, outgoing chord enhancement and same-prefix runtime behavior; no request for diagnostic ZIP or broad .NET runtime reinstall is justified by current evidence.

confidence.rationale: Exact extracted method, native action/second-key source and reporter screenshot support the editor mechanism. Installed editor behavior, release-source identity and overlapping-shortcut runtime precedence remain unverified.

verification: Enabled incoming chords expose a second-action dropdown after Apps/Menu and preserve X through edit/save/reopen; disabled chords and ordinary shortcuts retain their one-action behavior.
Keyboard capture and dropdown paths produce the same native first/second action representation; no unrelated mapping or shortcut action is rewritten.

Run the existing Keyboard Manager editor/native tests and an interactive editor smoke check. Current proof covers the exact collection method only, not installed rendering, serialization or hook precedence.
proposed_fixes.title: Preserve incoming shortcut chords in Keyboard Manager dropdown editing
plan: In src/modules/keyboardmanager/KeyboardManagerEditorUI/Controls/UnifiedMappingControl.xaml.cs, make trigger-side dropdown growth/shrink respect the existing incoming-chord policy: allow one second action key when chords are enabled, preserve it when editing the first action, cap action count at two, and retain ordinary modifier-plus-one-action behavior when disabled.

Keep trigger and action-side policy explicit. Do not accidentally enable unsupported outgoing chords, globally classify Apps/Menu as a modifier, or permit repeated modifier categories as part of this fix; related enhancement22752 and outgoing-chord request31891 are separate decisions.

Keep dropdown, key-capture hook and native Shortcut.SetKeyCodes serialization consistent. Round-trip an existing Shift(Right)+Apps/Menu+X mapping and create the same mapping from scratch without silently dropping X.

Add focused collection/validation tests for enabled and disabled chords, editing first versus second action, replacing an action with a modifier, the two-action cap, standard shortcuts and untouched sibling mappings.

Verify legacy chord and the shorter Shift(Right)+Apps/Menu mapping separately, then together. Record press/release order and actual precedence; change engine conflict handling only if that separate runtime defect is reproduced.
proposed_fixes.root_cause: UnifiedMappingControl.HandleAutoGrowShrink grows only for modifiers and trims all trailing keys when an action is selected. This bypasses the existing AllowChords/secondKey model and prevents selecting or preserving the second action key after Apps/Menu.
